_comment: Expansion 6 G.5: rumours, clues and found letters that lead somewhere (game/story/rumours.py). rumour_hook has {hook} {villain} {home} {town}; rumour_near and the letter the same without {hook} (no {where}: the storybook check fills only the tale's words); the clue tables have the tale's words and {who} or {place}.

rumour_hook: "You want to know what's wrong? I'll tell you." {hook}
They look about before they speak. "Nobody says it out loud, but everybody knows." {hook}
"If you're the sort who goes looking for trouble, there's trouble enough." {hook}
"I'll tell you, and you didn't hear it from me." {hook}
rumour_near: "There's talk of {villain}, out by {home}. Folk go the long way round now."
"Something's wrong at {home}. It's {villain}, they say, though nobody who's seen it says much."
"Keep clear of {home}. That's where {villain} is, and the ones who went to look didn't come back."
"My cousin swears {villain} is at {home}. He doesn't drink, my cousin. That's what frightens me."
rumour_clue_who: "You're after {villain}? Then you want {who}. Knows more than they let on, that one."
"Ask {who}. I've heard them talk about it when they think nobody's listening."
"If anyone knows what {villain} fears, it's {who}. Don't say I sent you."
rumour_clue_saw: "There's {who}. Saw it with their own eyes, and hasn't been the same since."
"Go and find {who}. They were there, that night. They'll tell you, if you ask kindly."
"There's one who saw it and lived: {who}. Ask them."
rumour_clue_place: "If it's {villain} you're after, look at {place}. That's where the trouble is."
"They've been seen at {place}. Not lately, but the tracks don't lie."
"Everyone who knows anything says the same thing: {place}. Go there, if you must."
letter_hook: The hand is cramped and hurried. It writes of {villain} at {home}, of the dead it left near {town}, and of how much the writer meant to be paid for it. It ends in the middle of a word.
Someone wrote this to the people of {town}: that they had found where {villain} lairs, at {home}, and would go in at first light. There is no signature, and no second letter.
A letter never sent. The writer had tracked {villain} to {home}, and knew {town} would pay for its end. The last lines are smudged, as if written in the rain, or in a hurry.
letter_den: Whoever wrote it never came back for it.
The road to {home} is drawn in the margin, in the same shaking hand.
At the bottom, in another hand: the people of {town} will pay well.
